note: Eight candidate strategies, written before any of them was scored, so the set cannot be trimmed to fit a result. Every market-facing field (line, price, ROI, CLV, leg correlation) is null because no verifiable price or leg-level sample exists in this repository. A null here is a finding, not a formatting choice.

strategies.name: Pythagorean expectation residual
strategies.hypothesis: Clubs whose win total runs ahead of their scoring profile (Pythagorean expectation from points for and against) are more likely to regress than clubs whose record matches their scoring profile. The candidate is a spread or moneyline position against the over-performing club.
strategies.inputs: Points for, points against, wins, losses, ties from the official league standings table.
strategies.output: Expected win total, residual wins, and a standardised residual per club (this page, derived).
strategies.test: Walk-forward: compute the residual from games 1..k, then evaluate the next block. Requires a per-week historical snapshot that this repository does not hold.
strategies.kills_it: If scoring-profile residual has no relationship to future point margin, the premise is empty.
strategies.risk: Regression-to-the-mean language is often used to justify a bet that the market has already priced. Without a price, the residual cannot be converted into an edge.

strategies.name: Scoring environment total
strategies.hypothesis: A club's own points for and points against per game, combined for both clubs in a fixture, gives a baseline expectation for the game total that can be compared with a posted total.
strategies.inputs: PF and PA per club from the official standings table; the Week 10 fixture list.
strategies.output: Baseline total estimate per fixture (derived on the Probability page once a historical archive exists).
strategies.test: Compare the baseline total with realised totals across many weeks, not one week.
strategies.kills_it: If the naive scoring average predicts totals as well as any adjusted model, the added complexity earns nothing.
strategies.risk: The baseline ignores opponent strength, pace, weather and venue. Its error is unknown until it is scored.

strategies.name: Availability shock
strategies.hypothesis: Clubs entering a fixture with more first-string players carrying a game status (Out, then Questionable) will under-perform their season baseline in that game, and their opponents will over-perform.
strategies.inputs: Week 10 official injury report; the three transcribed club depth charts; the fixture list.
strategies.output: Per-club report pressure counts and chart-level first-string affected players (this page).
strategies.test: Needs several weeks of injury reports archived with their report timestamps, joined to results.
strategies.kills_it: If the market moves on the same report before the price is available, the information is already in the number.
strategies.risk: A listed player is not necessarily a starter, and a depth chart is a coaching estimate rather than a lineup. Both facts are visible in this repository's data and are not smoothed over.

strategies.name: Replacement-chain erosion
strategies.hypothesis: When a club's published first-string player at a position is unavailable, the next listed player inherits opportunity. The prop candidate is usage (attempts, targets, carries) for the replacement, not a raw yardage projection.
strategies.inputs: Depth charts for the three clubs with transcribed charts; the official injury report.
strategies.output: Replacement chains per position, with the chart's own remainder list (this page).
strategies.test: Needs snap counts or per-game usage for replacements, which this repository does not hold.
strategies.kills_it: If the replacement's usage is priced identically to the starter's, the chain carries no information.
strategies.risk: Depth charts are unofficial and change without notice; a club site can list a player who does not play that role in the game plan.

strategies.name: Completion-percentage persistence
strategies.hypothesis: Club passing efficiency measured on a stable denominator (completions over attempts, and yards over attempts, computed from the same integers) is more persistent week to week than raw passing yards, and therefore more useful in a prop baseline.
strategies.inputs: Attempts, completions and the displayed completion percentage from the official team passing table.
strategies.output: Derived yards per attempt and completion rate per club (this page).
strategies.test: Needs week-by-week passing splits, which the site exposes only as a season-to-date table in this capture.
strategies.kills_it: If week-to-week autocorrelation is near zero, a season rate is not a projection.
strategies.risk: Attempt volume and game script drive raw yards far more than efficiency. A persistence finding about rates would not transfer to yardage props.

strategies.name: Cross-game combination screen
strategies.hypothesis: Legs drawn from different games are closer to independent than same-game legs, so a cross-game combination's fair price is closer to the product of its marginals. The candidate prices cross-game combinations only.
strategies.inputs: No leg-level price or result archive exists here.
strategies.output: Nothing computed. The combination price fields are blank.
strategies.test: Requires a leg-level archive with prices taken at a known time.
strategies.kills_it: If even cross-game legs show measurable dependence through shared conditions (weather, referee crew, week-level effects), the product rule fails.
strategies.risk: Assuming independence because games look unrelated is exactly the assumption gate G05 exists to stop.

strategies.name: Same-game dependence penalty
strategies.hypothesis: Same-game legs are positively dependent when they share a side of the ball. A combination that quotes them as independent is over-priced relative to their true joint probability, which is a reason to avoid the combination rather than to bet it.
strategies.inputs: No same-game leg archive exists here.
strategies.output: Nothing computed. The measured leg correlation is blank.
strategies.test: Requires paired leg outcomes on the same game, which this repository does not hold.
strategies.kills_it: If measured same-game leg correlation is negligible, the penalty disappears and the hypothesis is empty.
strategies.risk: This is the one area where an honest research project can produce a useful conclusion that is simply 'do not buy this product'.

strategies.name: Team-total and receiver combination
strategies.hypothesis: A receiver's yardage prop and the club's team total share a common driver (the passing game). The candidate measures that dependence before quoting any joint probability.
strategies.inputs: Club passing totals from the official team table; no per-player game logs are held.
strategies.output: Nothing computed for the combination. Club-level correlation between passing yards and points is reported separately as descriptive only.
strategies.test: Requires per-player game logs and team totals on the same games.
strategies.kills_it: If the two legs show no measurable shared variation beyond the club's own scoring level, no combination premium exists.
strategies.risk: Club-level correlation is not a player-leg correlation. Re-using it as one would be the exact error gate G05 names.
